Q1. Which of the following statements is correct?
A. We can treat a bicycle wheel as a point mass when studying how the spokes
flex as it rolls.
This is incorrect because spoke flex depends on the wheel’s size and shape, so a point-mass
model throws away the needed geometry.
B. We can reasonably treat a delivery van as a point mass when estimating how
far it travels across town in 15 minutes.
For city-scale motion, the van’s size is tiny compared with the travel distance, so a point-mass
approximation captures its position change well.
C. We are not allowed to assume motion in a vacuum even if we want to neglect
air resistance in a first-pass calculation.
This is incorrect because “ignore air resistance” is essentially the same modeling step as treating
the situation like a vacuum for that effect.
D. None of the above is correct.
This is incorrect because one of the statements (about using a point-mass model over large
distances) is a valid approximation.

constant.

Q7. A tennis ball is launched with speed u0 at an angle α above the horizontal
(ignore air resistance). What is the speed of the ball when it is at its maximum
height?
A. u0.
This is incorrect because the vertical component of velocity decreases to zero at the top, reducing
the speed from its launch value.
B. u0 cos α.
This is correct because at maximum height the vertical velocity is zero, so the speed equals the
unchanged horizontal component u0 cos α.
C. u0 sin α.
This is incorrect because u0 sin α is the initial vertical component, which is not the speed at the
peak.
D. 0.
This is incorrect because although the vertical velocity is zero at the top, the horizontal velocity
is still nonzero.

A. A more massive spacecraft needs a larger escape speed from the same planet.
This is incorrect because the spacecraft’s mass does not appear in v =

B. A planet with the same mass but a larger radius has a larger escape speed.
This is incorrect because increasing R makes 2GM/R smaller, lowering the escape speed.

smaller R both push v upward.

Q12. A 3.2 kg cart initially moving at 1.8 m/s collides with a wall and rebounds
at a speed of 0.6 m/s moving backward. The collision lasts for 0.15 seconds.
What is the average force exerted on the cart during the collision?
A. 51.2 N
This is correct because Favg = ∆p/∆t = m(vf − vi)/∆t = 3.2(−0.6 − 1.8)/0.15 = −51.2 N, so
the magnitude is 51.2 N.
B. 38.4 N
This is incorrect because it treats the velocity change as (−0.6)−(−1.8) or otherwise mishandles
the sign for a rebound.
C. 64.0 N
This is incorrect because it uses an incorrect velocity change or divides by the wrong collision
time.
D. 7.68 N
This is incorrect because it computes impulse |∆p| but forgets to divide by the collision duration
to get force.
